package_info.package_versions: Unknown (affects all sites using the compromised provider's code)
package_info.why_malicious: The JavaScript code distributed by a trusted media content provider was compromised to deliver FakeUpdates malware to over 250 media websites, resulting in widespread drive-by malware distribution.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when user visits affected media website)
execution_context.file_location: Injected/compromised JavaScript file loaded from media content provider CDN

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code loads and executes a remote JavaScript payload from a malicious domain, which then attempts to deliver FakeUpdates malware to site visitors.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code dynamically loads and executes a remote script from an untrusted, non-affiliated domain, a common technique for malware delivery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal third-party JavaScript should not inject or execute code from unknown external sources, especially those unrelated to the media provider.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use might include loading analytics or ad scripts from known, vetted partners, but not from random or newly registered domains.
key_indicators: External domain not associated with the media provider
Behavior matches known FakeUpdates (SocGholish) delivery patterns

attack_chain.action: Threat actor compromises JavaScript code at a trusted media content provider.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious JavaScript is distributed to all websites using the provider.

attack_chain.action: Compromised JavaScript is loaded by over 250 media websites, executing in visitors' browsers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious script loads additional payload from attacker's infrastructure.

attack_chain.action: Malicious payload (FakeUpdates) is delivered to end users, potentially leading to further malware infection.
attack_chain.leads_to: User systems are infected with FakeUpdates malware.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected runtime injection of external scripts from non-affiliated domains
JavaScript code dynamically creating <script> tags with remote sources
Network requests to known FakeUpdates/SocGholish infrastructure
file_indicators: JavaScript files from trusted providers suddenly referencing new, unknown domains
Injected script tags in the DOM pointing to suspicious URLs
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains associated with SocGholish/FakeUpdates
Unusual traffic from media websites to newly registered or flagged malicious domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for changes in third-party JavaScript loaded by your site, especially new or unexpected external script sources. Use web application firewalls or browser security tools to block or alert on dynamic script injection from untrusted domains. Analyze network traffic for connections to known FakeUpdates/SocGholish infrastructure. Regularly audit the integrity of JavaScript dependencies and CDN-hosted assets.
